A properly sized grounding/bonding conductor should be installed from the main electrical service to the water piping system near the water meter. This provides a proper path for fault current and helps reduce the risk of electrical shock when using metal plumbing fixtures.

Today, I arrived at the Themis residence to perform a complimentary electrical system check. Upon arrival, the homeowner informed me of several electrical concerns she wanted me to evaluate, including an issue with the dryer and a dining room light that was not functioning properly.

Upon evaluating the dryer, I found that the dryer itself appears to have an internal failure or a failed component, which is causing it not to operate properly. The issue does not appear to be related to the home’s electrical supply.

The homeowner also reported that the dining room light had stopped working after she reset the breaker. I proceeded to the electrical panel to inspect the breakers, voltages, and connections. Upon inspection, I found that both 200-amp main electrical panels are enclosed within a cabinet and are currently inaccessible because they are completely stuck within the cabinet.

The two main electrical panels are original to the home and are over 35 years old. Due to their age, there is an increased likelihood of breaker and other component failures, which can contribute to electrical distribution problems and potential safety concerns. The panels are Sylvania panels, which are known to have issues with breakers failing to trip properly under certain fault conditions. A breaker that fails to trip when required can allow excessive current to continue flowing, potentially resulting in overheating or damage to connected electrical components.

Based on the age, condition, accessibility, and manufacturer of the existing equipment, I informed homeowner both 200-amp main electrical panels need to be replaced to improve electrical safety, reliability, and proper power distribution throughout the home.

I also explained that the existing cabinet will need to be modified or removed as necessary to provide proper access when the panels are replaced. In addition, surge protection will need to be installed at the main panels as part of the panel replacement to meet current code requirements. Themis didn’t want anything els checked during today visit.

A surge protection device installed at the main electrical panel helps protect electrical equipment throughout the home from power surges caused by internal sources, such as large appliances cycling on and off, utility power fluctuations, and storms.

I recommended installing a whole-home surge protection device at the main electrical panel to provide protection for the home’s electrical equipment.

I also found that the photocell controlling the lamp post was no longer functioning. Because the photocell is integrated into the lamp post, I recommended either installing an in-wall timer or removing the photocell. I removed the photocell, after which the light began functioning properly.

invoices.summary:
This estimate includes having Lancaster Plumbing and Heating make a warranty repair on the water softener. It would include removal of the mechanical parts of the head that control the stages of the water softeners regeneration. This repair is covered under both the manufacturer’s parts warranty and Lancaster Plumbing and Heating’s labor warranty.

We came out today to take a look at the water softener because it was showing an error code. The error code was indicating that there was a motor failure. This usually means that during regeneration the computer was telling the spacer stack assembly to switch positions and it took too long or got stuck.

The technician began diagnosing the issue by disconnecting power and trying a hard reset of the electrical components. This did not fix the issue, so the technician provided an estimate to perform a warranty repair. The warranty repair included replacing the spacer stack assembly, and the motor that drives the functions for the spacer stack assembly. Once the repair was completed, the technician put the water softener through an abbreviated regeneration twice in order to verify that the system was now working properly. Both attempts on the abbreviated regeneration were successful and everything was in proper operation at this time.

The technician did discover a secondary issue, but it had to do with the Brian tank. The homeowners have been using salt pellets instead of salt crystals, and this is caused bridging within the brine tank. The technician suggested that the salt be dug out of the brine tank in order to fix this issue. Moving forward we did recommend the use of salt crystals because they do dissolve easier with these particular systems.

If you have any other questions or concerns that arise after today’s visit, please do not hesitate to give us a call. Thank you for continuing to trust Lancaster Plumbing and Heating with all of your home service needs.
